method: score = band_width x habitat_weight x mixed_fraction; greedy top 10 with kernel re-scoring over atmosphere distance, gravity (2 m/s^2), vent flow (10 cm/s) and CO2 fraction (0.10)

candidate_types.atmosphere: every grid point x metric M1-M3, habitat diluent N2

dilution.why: FLEX dilution tests were all at 13-25% O2; CO2 suppression at 34% O2 is gated

items.rationale: Extinction diameter at Moon gravity (0.165 g), 8.2 psia / 34% O2, vent 20 cm/s: there is no microgravity evidence at this atmosphere (honesty gate), 100% of physics samples are in the mixed regime where neither 0 g nor 1 g data apply, and the atmosphere is close to the lunar/Mars base 8.2 psia / 34% O2 target (weight 1.00).

Dilution at high O2: P(droplet flame self-extinguishes before burnout) with 40% CO2 replacing nitrogen at Moon gravity (0.165 g), 8.2 psia / 34% O2, vent 20 cm/s. FLEX tested CO2 dilution only at 14-24% O2, so the suppression calculator has no evidence here (honesty gate); 100% of physics samples are in the mixed regime, and the atmosphere is the lunar/Mars base 8.2 psia / 34% O2 target (weight 1.00). A droplet test here tells whether CO2 suppression works the same way in oxygen-enriched cabin air.

design_implications: At lunar gravity a 10 mm flame stays forced-flow dominated (Ri < 0.1, where microgravity evidence transfers) only above about 80 cm/s of vent flow at the median coefficients, and above 139 cm/s to cover 95% of the Monte Carlo samples (u_b p50 25.4 cm/s, p95 43.8 cm/s). Typical cabin vents (5-20 cm/s) are far below this, so lunar fires are mixed or buoyancy-dominated.

At lunar gravity a 10 mm flame becomes buoyancy-dominated (Ri > 10) when the vent flow is below about 8.0 cm/s (median coefficients): turning ventilation off does not create a microgravity-like quiescent flame.

At Mars gravity a 10 mm flame stays forced-flow dominated (Ri < 0.1, where microgravity evidence transfers) only above about 122 cm/s of vent flow at the median coefficients, and above 210 cm/s to cover 95% of the Monte Carlo samples (u_b p50 38.4 cm/s, p95 66.3 cm/s). Typical cabin vents (5-20 cm/s) are far below this, so Mars fires are mixed or buoyancy-dominated.

At Mars gravity a 10 mm flame becomes buoyancy-dominated (Ri > 10) when the vent flow is below about 12.2 cm/s (median coefficients): turning ventilation off does not create a microgravity-like quiescent flame.

Droplet and gas-burner extinction evidence (M1-M3) has no flow variable, so for partial-gravity habitats its bands are widened rather than shifted; tests in the mixed regime at 8.2 psia / 34% O2 are the most valuable way to narrow them.
